review: Every printed size/range row transcribed and visually compared with the rendered B550 page, retaining exact yard fractions. Existing whole-yard helper is only partial integration. Lower-bound policy, detailed combat/sense contracts and independent tests remain pending.

entries.acceptance: Size and speed/range use the same linear progression with opposite modifier signs. The selected size and movement inputs remain separate until their modifiers are combined.
entries.validation_note: Pure numeric helper with explicit dimension/shape/speed choices authored; tests unrun and combat/sense integration pending.

entries.acceptance: Use an explicitly supplied character, creature or vehicle size modifier rather than recalculating it from a rough descriptive height. Human baseline size is zero.
For an unspecified size modifier, use longest dimension and round up to the next printed threshold; for an object much smaller in two dimensions, use its smallest dimension instead.
entries.validation_note: Pure numeric helper with explicit dimension/shape/speed choices authored; tests unrun and combat/sense integration pending.

entries.acceptance: Box-like, spherical or amorphous bodies add two to the dimensional size modifier; elongated boxes add one. Shape is explicit authored geometry, not inferred from an object name.
entries.validation_note: Pure numeric helper with explicit dimension/shape/speed choices authored; tests unrun and combat/sense integration pending.

entries.acceptance: Range inputs between thresholds round upward. No range bonus applies within two yards; the range modifier remains zero even for smaller distances.
Ordinary on-foot combat and stationary objects normally ignore target speed. When the author determines fast motion matters, add speed in yards per second to range in yards before lookup.
entries.validation_note: Pure numeric helper with explicit dimension/shape/speed choices authored; tests unrun and combat/sense integration pending.

entries.acceptance: Moving-platform attacks use the detailed apparent relative-speed rule; adding the target's absolute world velocity unconditionally would conflict with B469.
Beyond the printed range, multiplying linear distance by ten changes size by +6 or range penalty by -6. Define the supported numeric range and reject overflow before multiplication.

Use exact inch/foot/yard conversion for small sizes. The table's parenthetical mile labels are approximate; its yard thresholds are the lookup values and must not be silently replaced with exact statutory-mile distances.
The table may also apply to sensing or other authored tasks when size/speed/range is relevant, but does not automatically replace each sensory trait's distinct range rules.
The printed smallest row is one-fifth inch. Before supporting smaller dimensions, establish the applicable extrapolation policy rather than silently clamping every tiny object to the same size.
Eight yards rounds to ten and yields range -4; forty yards plus thirty yards/second yields -9; five yards plus one thousand yards/second rounds to fifteen hundred and yields -17.
A four-yard longest dimension gives size +2 for the stated humanoid example, +3 for an elongated vehicle and +4 for a box-like building.
A six-yard-long target at forty yards moving fifteen yards/second has size +3 and speed/range -9, yielding a combined -6 before other attack modifiers.
